messages.subject: INLA crashing, no further output
parts:
Hi again,

Sorry for posting twice in one day-- this is regarding a different project, I think the issue with the first one is resolved (running now). 

I'm getting the following error message when running the code attached below:

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

I'm running with verbose=TRUE, but there is no further output. cattle_data is a spatial points data frame, num.cattle is a count/integer, as is clustermembers.cattle. My goal here is continuous mapping. 

Any guidance would be appreciated. 

Julianne

-------------------------------
coords<-cattle_data@coords #6,599 coordinates
loc = as.matrix(coords)
loc.mesh = loc
mesh = inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain = loc.mesh, 
                    max.edge = c(0.3,0.6), 
                    offset = c(1, 1))
A<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc=coords)
spde_RE<-inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha=2) 
iset <- inla.spde.make.index('i', n.spde=spde_RE$n.spde)#no ST interaction

stk.dat.c<-inla.stack(
  data=list(resp=cattle_data@data$num.cattle), 
  A=list(A,1), 
  effects=list(iset,
  data.frame(intercept = rep(1, nrow(cattle_data@data)),
             urban=cattle_data@data$urban)), 
  tag='est')

f.spde.urb <- resp ~ 0 + intercept + urban + f(i, model=spde_RE) 
res.spde.c.urb<-inla (f.spde.urb, data=inla.stack.data(stk.dat.c), family="zeroinflatedpoisson1", offset=log(cattle_data@data$clustermembers.cattle), control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.dat.c)), 
                      num.threads = inla.getOption("num.threads"), control.compute=list(config = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)
